claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist that also inhibits CDK1, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on CDK1 activity and/or beta-adrenergic signaling. Lines with intact cell-cycle checkpoints (e.g., TP53 wild-type) and low CDK1 expression may be less sensitive, while those with high CDK1 expression or loss of checkpoint control (e.g., TP53 mutation) are more sensitive. The observed sensitivity in lines with KRAS, BRAF, or PIK3CA mutations suggests that oncogenic signaling may upregulate CDK1 or create dependence on beta-adrenergic pathways.

features.basis: Isoxsuprine inhibits CDK1 (IC50 2.9 µM); high CDK1 expression may predict sensitivity.
Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist; high ADRB2 expression may mediate its effects.
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, suggesting loss of checkpoint control enhances CDK1 dependence.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may upregulate CDK1 or beta-adrenergic signaling.
BRAF mutations are present in sensitive lines (e.g., AM38, IGR37) and may increase CDK1 activity.
PIK3CA mutations are enriched in sensitive lines and may promote CDK1 dependence.
PTEN mutations appear in sensitive lines and may activate PI3K/AKT signaling, increasing CDK1 activity.
ARID1A mutations are more frequent in least-affected lines, suggesting a protective role.
NF1 mutations appear in several least-affected lines, possibly reducing sensitivity.
SF3B1 mutations are common in least-affected lines, suggesting a protective association.
SMARCA4 mutations appear in least-affected lines, possibly indicating reduced sensitivity.
CDKN2A mutations are present in several sensitive lines, suggesting loss of cell-cycle inhibition enhances CDK1 dependence.
